action: Customers of JPMorgan, Mastercard and Visa programs: expect phishing that uses your name or email, and do not act on unsolicited messages.
date_note: Date of the companies' statements: ABC13 (read 2026-11-19) says JPMorganChase made its statement Thursday morning (19 November); the date of the attack itself is not stated.
exec: Vendor incidents reached marketing data held for major banking and card brands; customers face phishing risk.
plain: Visa, JPMorgan and Mastercard say outside vendors were hacked. JPMorgan says some customer names and email addresses may be exposed; Mastercard says a limited amount of cardholder emails were. Visa says its systems were not affected, and Mastercard says its payment network was not.
summary: JPMorganChase said attackers accessed marketing data held by its vendors that may include some customer names and email addresses, and it will offer free credit monitoring where appropriate. Visa tied the claims to an Asia Pacific provider; Mastercard cited a limited amount of cardholder emails. n0n claimed the data; Reuters, per SecurityWeek, found over 16,000 customer emails. SOCRadar, per The Register, found no card numbers or passwords in the 14 published files.
title: Visa, JPMorgan and Mastercard say third-party providers were hit; n0n gang claims it, per Reuters and SOCRadar

validation.note: Company statements read in Yahoo Finance, ABC13 and SecurityWeek. The n0n claim is the group's, relayed by Reuters (SecurityWeek) and SOCRadar (Yahoo, which says SOCRadar has not verified it). The Register (read 20 November) relays SOCRadar CISO Ensar Seker on the content of the published files; this is SOCRadar's review, not the companies'.

review.note: Compared with Yahoo, SecurityWeek, The Register: statements, Asia Pacific provider, 16,000 (Reuters via SecurityWeek), SOCRadar 14 files match.
